facts.statement: Banguela is an extinct azhdarchoid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous period found in modern-day Brazil.
facts.quote: Banguela is a genus of azhdarchoid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous period (Albian stage) of what is now Brazil.

facts.statement: Only one species of Banguela is known to science, Banguela oberlii.
facts.quote: Only one species is known, Banguela oberlii.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was acquired by Swiss collector Urs Oberli from the Chapada do Araripe region.
facts.quote: The Swiss collector Urs Oberli acquired a pterosaur jaw fragment from the Chapada do Araripe.

facts.statement: In 2005, André Jacques Veldmeijer and colleagues described the fossil as a species of Thalassodromeus.
facts.quote: In 2005, this was described by André Jacques Veldmeijer and colleagues, and referred to Thalassodromeus sethi.

facts.statement: Jaime Headden and Hebert Bruno Nascimento Campos named and described Banguela as a separate genus in 2015.
facts.quote: In 2015, it was named and described by Jaime Headden and Hebert Bruno Nascimento Campos as a separate genus Banguela, with the type species Banguela oberlii.

facts.statement: The genus name Banguela comes from a Brazilian Portuguese word meaning "toothless one," often used affectionately for elderly women.
facts.quote: The generic name is a Brazilian Portuguese word for "toothless one", especially used as an affectionate term for elderly women.

facts.statement: The species name oberlii honors the collector Urs Oberli.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Oberli.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen NMSG SAO 251093 was found in the Romualdo Formation and dates to the Albian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, NMSG SAO 251093, was probably found in the Romualdo Formation, also known as the Romualdo Member of the Santana Formation, dating from the Albian.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of the symphysis, or fused front end, of the lower jaws.
facts.quote: It consists of the symphysis, fused front end, of the lower jaws.

facts.statement: Banguela had an estimated skull length of about 2 feet and a wingspan of over 12 feet.
facts.quote: Banguela has an estimated skull length of about 2 ft and wingspan of over 12 ft.

facts.statement: The preserved symphysis measures 273 mm in length and curves upwards with a short depression at the upper rear end.
facts.quote: The symphysis, with a preserved length of 273 mm, curves upwards and has a relatively short depression at its upper rear end.

facts.statement: The front bottom edge of the symphysis is sharp but lacks a true crest.
facts.quote: The front bottom edge is sharp too but lacks a true crest.

facts.statement: The fossil fragment contains no teeth or tooth sockets.
facts.quote: There are no teeth or tooth sockets present in the fragment.

facts.statement: In 2015, Headden and Campos classified Banguela in the family Dsungaripteridae in a basal position.
facts.quote: In 2015, Headden & Campos placed Banguela in the family Dsungaripteridae, in a basal position.

facts.statement: Researchers disputed the classification of Banguela as a dsungaripterid because no unambiguous traits of that group were found in the type specimen.
facts.quote: However, its identity as a dsungaripterid was disputed by other researchers, since no unambiguous traits of dsungaripterids were found in the type specimen.

facts.statement: A 2018 study suggested Banguela was actually a species of Thalassodromeus and assigned it to the clade Thalassodromidae.
facts.quote: In 2018, a study suggested that Banguela was a species of Thalassodromeus (T. oberlii), and thus it is assigned to the clade Thalassodromidae.

facts.statement: In 2020, McPhee and colleagues argued that Banguela is a valid genus belonging to the Chaoyangopteridae.
facts.quote: In 2020, McPhee and colleagues considered Banguela as a valid genus, and claimed that it belongs to the Chaoyangopteridae.

facts.statement: Banguela lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Inferior

facts.statement: The holotype dates from the Aptian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: Su holotipo, el espécimen NMSG SAO 251093, fue hallado en la Formación Romualdo, también conocida como el Miembro Romualdo de la Formación Santana, que data de las etapas Aptiense al Albiense.

facts.statement: Banguela is unique among dsungaripteroid pterosaurs due to its total absence of teeth.
facts.quote: Banguela es único entre los pterosaurios dsungaripteroides debido a su total ausencia de dientes.

facts.statement: Tooth loss likely evolved independently at least four times among pterosaurs, as seen in groups like pteranodontids, nyctosaurids, and azhdarchoids.
facts.quote: Otros pterosaurios, como los pteranodóntidos, nictosáuridos y azdarcoideos, también perdieron sus dientes, lo que indica que esta condición apareció de manera independiente al menos cuatro veces entre los pterosaurios.

facts.statement: If tooth loss occurred frequently, Banguela may indicate it developed via the growth of horned rhamphothecae and progressive tooth reduction until teeth became useless.
facts.quote: Si este fuera el caso, entonces Banguela podría indicar como apareció esta condición en la mayoría de los casos: el desarrollo de una ranfoteca en las puntas de las mandíbulas, con una progresiva reducción dental hasta que los dientes cesaran de ser útiles.

facts.statement: Banguela lived between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)
